atlas-is.0111: After a degree from an Icelandic university: up to 18 months (reduced from three years in July 2026) to find specialist work, which converts it from inside Iceland. PhD graduates get 12 months more on their specialist permit.
atlas-is.0113: A degree or certified specialist training linked to the job and a contract at the collective-agreement rate; no labour-market test, a spouse may work at once, and permanent residence after four years (three with an Icelandic PhD).
atlas-is.0115: The employer applies after advertising with the labour directorate and EURES and finding no Icelandic or EEA candidate; the union checks the pay. You wait abroad; the permit lasts a year, renewable once, and does not lead to permanent residence.
atlas-is.0116: Visiting researchers can get a short-stay permit for 90 to 180 days; scholarship holders a special-purpose permit; researchers employed by a university the specialist permit. Teaching or conferences up to four weeks a year need no work permit.
atlas-is.0117: A PhD on a scholarship comes as a student; a salaried PhD as a specialist, with permanent residence after three years.
atlas-is.0119: UK citizens aged 18 to 30 can get 12 months, renewable once, with an unrestricted work permit included, as long as work stays secondary to the holiday.
atlas-is.0120: Iceland has youth-mobility agreements only with the UK, Canada, Japan, Andorra and Chile.
atlas-is.0121: For citizens of Canada, Japan, Andorra and Chile aged 18 to 30: 12 months, renewable once except for Japanese citizens, who pay no fee.
atlas-is.0122: Up to 90 days in any 180 with no work. Applying for a permit while visa-free does not stop the 90-day clock: past day 90 without a decision you are unlawfully present.
atlas-is.0123: Rent only a flat registered as a dwelling and without a clause banning registration: a lease in a commercial or industrial building cannot be your legal domicile and is grounds for refusing a permit.
atlas-is.0124: If you need a visa, you may not wait in Iceland while a first application is decided; if you are visa-free, applying does not stop your 90 Schengen days. Get the criminal record and translations apostilled.
atlas-is.0125: Staying over 3 months, register with Registers Iceland: form A-260 for your right of residence and A-270 for your domicile, with your work contract; students use form A-271 within 3 months, with enrolment, a statement of funds and the European Health Insurance Card. It is free.
atlas-is.0126: Register your legal domicile with Registers Iceland (forms A-270 or A-271) once the permit is approved: it unlocks housing benefit and starts the clock for public health cover.
atlas-is.0127: None beyond the registration: EEA citizens get no residence card.
atlas-is.0128: There is no biometrics desk at Keflavík airport: book an appointment at the Directorate of Immigration’s service centre to give photo and fingerprints for the residence card.
atlas-is.0129: Citizens of non-EEA Europe (including the UK), Asia, Africa and Latin America must have a medical check for infectious diseases after arriving before the permit and card are issued.
atlas-is.0130: US citizens are exempt from the medical check required of many other nationalities.
atlas-is.0131: Your national ID number (kennitala) comes with the EEA registration, or is generated for others after biometrics and permit approval; state, university and contract systems all use it.
atlas-is.0132: Show the S1 (or E104) form on arrival for immediate public cover; students use the European Health Insurance Card.
atlas-is.0133: Public cover starts after 3 months of registered domicile (6 months before 1 August 2026); until then you need private insurance of at least 2,000,000 ISK, valid from the day you register.
atlas-is.0134: Get the electronic ID (rafræn skilríki) in person with your kennitala, passport and an Icelandic phone number: it opens island.is, the health portal, the tax office and online banking. Banks then open an account with your kennitala, passport, proof of domicile and work or study contract.
atlas-is.0135: Apply to renew on island.is at least 4 weeks before your card expires: a late application is treated as a first one, ending your right to work and resetting the 4 years counted towards permanent residence. Students must pass 75% of a year’s credits to renew.
atlas-is.0136: Renew at least four weeks before your card expires: a late application is treated as a first one, stopping your right to work and resetting the years towards permanent residence.
atlas-is.0137: Private health insurance must cover at least ISK 2,000,000 from the day you register your address; non-EEA arrivals get public cover after three months.
atlas-is.0138: A lease in a commercial building, or one forbidding registration, blocks your address registration and permit.
atlas-is.0139: Criminal records and translations without an apostille are a common reason for refusal.
atlas-is.0140: Public universities may charge non-EEA students tuition from autumn 2027; the fee tables are not yet set.
atlas-is.0141: Work permits moved from the labour directorate to ÚTL on 8 July 2026, slowing first applications this autumn.
atlas-is.0142: Newcomers without an Icelandic biometric passport wait three to six weeks for an in-person bank appointment to activate the electronic ID.
atlas-is.0143: Many Reykjavík landlords still rent off the books and refuse address registration.
